changelog: - **Projects are scoped to the caller's tenant on every route and on the detail page** (#2622, noticed during #2618). With `MT_ENFORCE_ISOLATION` off the org middleware scopes nothing, and every project rule (`canViewProject`, `isProjectOwner`, `canManageProject`) answers true for any ADMIN — so an admin of one org listed every org's projects (`GET /api/projects`, whose ADMIN scope is `{}`; mentees and sources likewise saw every org's public ones), and could read, edit, delete, and manage the roster, join requests, goal templates and goals of another org's project by id; the `/projects/[id]` page gave them the full internal view, private projects included. Now: the list ANDs the role scope with `tenantWhere(session)`; each of the 13 handlers under `/api/projects/[id]/**` asks the new `projectInCallerTenant()` first and answers another tenant's project with the same 404 body as a missing one; `members` POST and `resolveOwner()` resolve the user/company in the caller's tenant (another tenant's is a 400, so no foreign member or owner, and no name read back); `POST /api/projects` stamps `orgId` itself (with the flag off nothing does, and a NULL-org project is the default org's — it would have vanished from its own creator's now-scoped list); and the page reads a signed-in visitor from another tenant exactly like an anonymous one (public stub or 404). The cross-tenant public showcase `/projects` is unchanged; `/api/project-tasks/[taskId]` was already tenant-checked. New `e2e/cross-tenant-projects.spec.ts` (verified failing on the previous code).
